name: Siha
title: Temple Servant After the Exile
summary: Siha (also spelled Siaha) was the ancestor of a family of temple servants (Nethinim) who returned from the Babylonian exile to Jerusalem. His descendants are mentioned among those who served at the temple after its rebuilding. Although he is a lesser-known biblical figure, his mention shows that temple service was restored with great accuracy after the exile.

keyEvents.title: Listed Among the Temple Servants in the Book of Ezra
keyEvents.description: Siha's descendants are listed among the temple servants (Nethinim) who returned to Jerusalem from Babylon under Zerubbabel's leadership.

keyEvents.title: Listed Among the Temple Servants in the Book of Nehemiah
keyEvents.description: In Nehemiah's parallel list of those who returned from exile, Siha's descendants are again mentioned among the temple servants.

keyEvents.title: The Return from Babylon
keyEvents.description: Siha's family was among the many families of temple servants who followed Zerubbabel back to the Promised Land to rebuild the temple and restore worship.

keyEvents.title: The Role of Temple Servants in the Rebuilding
keyEvents.description: The temple servants, including the descendants of Shallum, settled in their towns and contributed to rebuilding religious life in Jerusalem after the exile.
